uncertainties: The profile centres on Conservative leadership and premiership, 1975–1990. Earlier 1967 votes provide context; later retirement statements, including later climate scepticism, do not override the premiership record.

Answers are editorial reconstructions, not answers given by Thatcher. AI, cryptocurrencies, facial recognition, gender self-identification, neutral language, cultivated meat and enhancement questions are modern hypotheticals. Qualified choices extrapolate from documented principles; neutral answers retain unresolved tensions rather than claim a historical position.

UK constitutional analogies matter: opposition to devolved legislatures is distinct from opposition to European supranational authority. Parliamentary sovereignty explains representacao_05; accepting judicial review of executive acts does not establish support for courts striking down Acts of Parliament.

Local services and police were not all nationalised. School-level choice and administration qualify centralising answers. estrutura_18 rejects the absolute ban on any consensual separation rather than endorsing unilateral Scottish independence.

Broadcasting restrictions concerned specified organisations and direct speech; they did not outlaw all press criticism. National-security union restrictions and lawful interception should not be described as unlimited police power. poder_19 rejects detention with no defined endpoint or trial; it does not deny support for special counterterrorism powers.

Death-penalty support concerned exceptionally grave murders, not an automatic death sentence for every crime mentioned in poder_15. Firearms proposals restricted specified weapons and preserved licensed sporting uses; this is not a total civilian firearms ban.

The economic record includes a publicly funded NHS, pensions and basic welfare. economia_14 is a qualified inference from work incentives and conditional assistance, not a claim that she imposed a universal fixed benefit time limit.

controle_17 reflects retained national monetary authority and the ability to manage exchange arrangements; it does not claim uninterrupted support for fixed exchange rates. The 1990 ERM decision does not erase earlier opposition to monetary integration.

Publicly funded religious education and Christian moral language do not imply a theocracy. Moral reconstruction distinguishes private decriminalisation, public promotion, adoption and marriage. No claim is made that modern gender or language proposals existed in their present form during her premiership.

Embryo division: amendment 1 would have prohibited research; Thatcher voted No, then Aye on the clause. Support for licensed early-embryo research does not imply support for unrestricted cloning or selecting intelligence and appearance. Clinical devices and therapeutic research are distinguished from enhancement.

Environmental answers use her 1988 scientific and policy statements, including efficiency and pollution control. Agricultural biotechnology, urban/rural preferences and modern food technologies are not presented as direct quotations or documented questionnaire answers.
distinctions: Likely neighbours include Ronald Reagan and John Howard: Thatcher shared market reform and Atlantic security priorities, but governed a unitary parliamentary system, retained the NHS and supported specified gun restrictions. Assess independently; do not copy their answers.
Unlike protectionist nationalist profiles, opposition to European political centralisation coexisted with support for the European single market, foreign investment and global trade.

Unlike a libertarian minimum-state profile, she retained public welfare, national monetary accountability and coercive policing; unlike a theocratic conservative profile, she supported limited abortion law reform and licensed embryo research.
Unlike an unconditional interventionist, she disputed the Grenada invasion and broad South African economic sanctions. Those differences do not make her neutralist or pacifist.

Reviewed the 96.7% Howard warning: Thatcher’s stored model differs especially on religion (17.6 versus 36.5) and immigration (68.2 versus 54.0). Her explicit Christian public ethos and 1978 migration programme support these directions. These numbers describe editorial models, not independently measured beliefs.

Reviewed the 96.4% Kristol warning: Thatcher’s model differs on representation (76.3 versus 57.5), structure (34.3 versus 51.2) and morality (29.1 versus 15.0). Her parliamentary commitments, anti-devolution position and qualified abortion record support keeping a distinct independently assessed profile.

similarityReview.reason: These distinct politicians share conservative, market and alliance commitments. Thatcher’s independent model is more centralised (estrutura 34.3 versus 54.5), more supportive of coercive law enforcement (poder 68.7 versus 59.1), more open to trade (comercio 21.0 versus 28.2), and less uniformly traditional on personal morality (moral 29.1 versus 19.6). Her opposition to the proposed Scottish Assembly, support for capital punishment, free-trade speeches and qualified abortion position support these differences. The figures compare editorial models, not measured beliefs. No answers were adjusted to reduce similarity.
